record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Give characterizations of Arnoux-Rauzy words with a given balance.

evidence.quote: Give characterizations of Arnoux-Rauzy words with a given balance.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An infinite word $w$ over a finite alphabet $A$ is called Arnoux–Rauzy if, for every length $n\ge 0$, $w$ has exactly one right special factor and exactly one left special factor of length $n$, and each of these special factors can be extended (on the appropriate side) by every letter of $A$. For an infinite word $w$ and an integer $C\ge 1$, $w$ is said to be $C$-balanced if for every letter $a\in A$ and every pair of factors $u,v$ of $w$ with $|u|=|v|$ one has $\bigl||u|_a-|v|_a\bigr|\le C$, where $|x|_a$ denotes the number of occurrences of $a$ in $x$. The balance of $w$ is the smallest such $C$ (or $\infty$ if no finite $C$ works).

Problem. Give a characterization, in terms of the directive sequence (the sequence of letters generating $w$ via the Arnoux–Rauzy substitutions), of those Arnoux–Rauzy words over an alphabet of size $k\ge 3$ that have a prescribed balance $C$. In particular, for each $C\ge 1$, describe explicitly the set of directive sequences producing $C$-balanced Arnoux–Rauzy words.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist: necessary and sufficient conditions for 2-balanced ternary Arnoux–Rauzy words have been obtained using the notion of strong C-balance, and it is known that for every C the set of directive sequences of C-balanced ternary Arnoux–Rauzy words is not a rational language, so no characterization purely in terms of regular languages is possible. A complete characterization for general C and arbitrary alphabet size remains open.

status_evidence.title: Balance properties of Arnoux-Rauzy words
status_evidence.snippet: Sufficient and necessary conditions for 2-balance via strong C-balance; the set of prefixes of directive sequences of 2-balanced ternary Arnoux-Rauzy words is not rational.
status_evidence.claim: Partial characterizations of balance for Arnoux-Rauzy words exist, but a full rational-language characterization is impossible.

status_evidence.title: Which Arnoux-Rauzy Words Are 2-Balanced?
status_evidence.snippet: Studies which Arnoux-Rauzy words are 2-balanced, providing partial characterizations.
status_evidence.claim: The 2-balanced case has been investigated with partial results.
